questions.q: If& ${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\left(5 + 2x - 2x^{2}\right)\left(1 + e\left(2 - 4x\right)\right)}dx = \dfrac{1}{α}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{β}\right), \alpha, \beta > 0$, then~${α}^{4} - {β}^{4}$& is equal to&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{ \left(5 + 2x - 2x^{2}\right) \left(1 + e \left(2 - 4x\right)\right)}$dx = $\dfrac{1}{α}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{β}\right)

Now let,

$I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{5}{2} - \left(x^{2} - x\right)\right)\left(1 + e^{- 4\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}\right)}$dx$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\left(\left(\dfrac{11}{4}\right) - \left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)2\right)\left(1 + e^{- 4\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}\right)}$dx$

Now let~$x - $\dfrac{1}{2} =$t ⇒ dx = dt$

So, integral becomes,

$I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{- 12}^{12}\dfrac{1}{\left\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{- 4t}\right)}$dt$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{- 12}^{0}\dfrac{1}{\left\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{- 4t}\right)}$dt + \mathop{\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{12}\dfrac{1}{\left\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{- 4t}\right)}$dt ⏟}_{I2}$

Now solving~${I}_{2} = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{- 12}^{12}\dfrac{1}{\left\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{- 4t}\right)}$dt$,~

Let~$t = - z$, we get~$dt = - dz$

So,~${I}_{2} = - $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{12}^{0}\dfrac{dz}{\left\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - z^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{4z}\right)}

$⇒ {I}_{2} = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{12}\dfrac{dt}{\left\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{4t}\right)}

Now putting the value of~{I}_{2}\text{in}$I$~we get,

$I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{12}\dfrac{1}{\left(\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{- 4t}\right)} + \dfrac{1}{\left(\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{4t}\right)}$dt$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{12}\dfrac{e4t}{\left(\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(e^{4t} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{1}{\left(\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}\right)\left(1 + e^{4t}\right)}$dt$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{12}\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)2 - t^{2}}$dt$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2\left(\dfrac{11}{2}\right)}{\ln \left|\dfrac{\dfrac{11}{2} + t}{\dfrac{11}{2} - t}\right|}_{0}^{12}

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2\ssqrt{11}}\ln \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11} +1}{\sqrt{11} -$1}$) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{11}}$\ln \left(\dfrac{( \sqrt{11} + 1{)}^{2}}{10})$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{11}ln $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11} + 1}{10})

Now on comparing with~\dfrac{1}{α}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{β})~we get,

$⇒ \alpha = $\sqrt{11}, \beta = \sqrt{10}$⇒ {α}^{4} - {β}^{4} = 21$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3}sec\dfrac{2}{3}x \cdot cosec\dfrac{4}{3}xdx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $I = {∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3}sec\dfrac{2}{3}x \cdot cosec\dfrac{4}{3}xdx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3}\left(\dfrac{1}{cos\dfrac{2}{3}x \cdot sin\dfrac{4}{3}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3}\left(\dfrac{\cos^{\dfrac{4}{3}}x}{\cos^{\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{4}{3}}x \cdot \sin^{\dfrac{4}{3}}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\pi6}^{\pi3} \left(\dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{\tan^{\dfrac{4}{3}}x}\right)dx$

Let $\tan x = t, { sec}^{2}xdx = dt$~and at~$x = \dfrac{π}{6}, t = \tan \left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$~and at~$x = \dfrac{π}{3}, t = \tan \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{1\sqrt{3}}^{3}\dfrac{dt}{t\dfrac{4}{3}}$

Using~$∫ x^{n}dx = \dfrac{xn + 1}{n + 1}$

$⇒ I = {\dfrac{t- \dfrac{4}{3} + 1}{- \dfrac{4}{3} + 1}}_{1\sqrt{3}}^{3}$

$⇒ I = {- 3t^{- \dfrac{1}{3}}}_{1\sqrt{3}}^{3}$

$⇒ I = - 3\left\{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)- \dfrac{1}{3} - \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)- \dfrac{1}{3}\right\}$

$⇒ I = - 3\left\{\left(3\dfrac{1}{2}\right)- \dfrac{1}{3} - \left(\dfrac{1}{3\dfrac{1}{2}}\right)- \dfrac{1}{3}\right\}$

$= - 3 \left(\dfrac{1}{3\dfrac{1}{6}} -$3$\dfrac{1}{6}\right)

=\dfrac{- 3}{3\dfrac{1}{6}} +$3 $\times$3$\dfrac{1}{6}

=3\dfrac{7}{6} --3\dfrac{5}{6} .$

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\int_0^{x^2} \frac{\mathrm{t}^2-8 \mathrm{t}+15}{\mathrme^{\mathrm{t}}} \mathrm{dt}, x \in \mathbf{R}$. Then the numbers of local maximum and local minimum points of $f$, respectively, are :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\int_0^{x^2} \frac{t^2-8 t+15}{e^t} d t, x \in \mathbb{R} \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{x^4-8 x^2+15}{e^{x^2}}(2 x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{2 \times\left(x^2-5\right)\left(x^2-3\right)}{e^{x^2}}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x(x+\sqrt{5})(x-\sqrt{5})(x+\sqrt{3})(x-\sqrt{3})=0 \end{aligned}$ By using wavy curve method
Number of local maximum $=2$ Number of local minimum $=3$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{7  \left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx$, where~\left[\cdot\right]$denotes the greatest integer function, is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{dx}{7\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]dx$

Let $\dfrac{1}{7} = k ⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1}k\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}k\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{12}^{1}k\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]dx + {∫}_{13}^{12}k\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]dx + {∫}_{14}^{13}k\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]dx + ⋯$

$⇒ I = k\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + k^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + k^{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) + ⋯$

$⇒ I = \left($k + $\dfrac{k2}{2} + \dfrac{k3}{3} +$⋯\right) - $\dfrac{1}{k} \left(\dfrac{k2}{2} + \dfrac{k3}{3} +⋯\right)$

$⇒ I = - \ln \left(1 - k\right) - $\dfrac{1}{k}\left[-\ln \left(1 - k\right) - k\right]$

$⇒ I = - ln\dfrac{6}{7} -7 \left[-ln\dfrac{6}{7} - \dfrac{1}{7}\right]\left($∵ k = $\dfrac{1}{7}\right)

$∴ I = 1 + $6ln\dfrac{6}{7}

questions.q: If ${\theta}_{1}$ and ${\theta}_{2}$ be respectively the smallest and the largest values of $\theta$ in \left(0, 2\pi\right) - \left\{\pi\right\}$ which satisfy the equation, $2\cot^{2}  \theta - \dfrac{5}{sin  \theta} + 4 = 0$ , then $\mathop{∫}_{{\theta}_{1}}^{{\theta}_{2}}\cos^{2}  3\thetad\theta$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$2\cot^{2} \theta - \dfrac{5}{sin \theta} + 4 = 0$
$\dfrac{2\cos^{2} \theta}{\sin^{2} \theta} - \dfrac{5}{sin \theta} + 4 = 0$
$2\cos^{2} \theta - 5sin \theta + 4\sin^{2} \theta = 0, sin \theta \ne 0$
$2\sin^{2} \theta - 5sin \theta + 2 = 0$
\left(2sin \theta - 1\right)\left(sin \theta - 2\right) = 0$
$sin \theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\theta = \dfrac{π}{6}, \dfrac{5\pi}{6};$~$\theta \in \left(0, 2\pi\right) - \left\{\pi\right\}$
$∴ \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{5\pi / 6}\cos^{2} 3\thetad\theta = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{5\pi / 6}\dfrac{1 + \cos 6\theta}{2}d\theta$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}{\theta + \dfrac{\sin 6\theta}{6}}_{x / 6}^{5\pi / 6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{π}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6}\left(0 - 0\right)\right] = \dfrac{1}{2} . \dfrac{4\pi}{6} = \dfrac{π}{3}

questions.q: Let $f, g: \left(0, \infty\right) \to R$ be two functions defined by $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{- x}^{x}\left(\left|t\right| - t^{2}\right)e^{- t^{2}}dt and $g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x2}t\dfrac{1}{2}e^{- t^{2}}dt$. Then the value of $9 \left(f  \left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9} +g \left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9}\right\right))is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x2}t\dfrac{1}{2}e^{- t}dt$

Let, $t = y^{2}$

$⇒ dt = 2ydy$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}2y^{2}e^{- y^{2}}dy$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}t^{2}e^{- t^{2}}dt$

Also, $f\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}\left(t - t^{2}\right)e^{- t^{2}}dt$y

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}te^{- t^{2}}dt$

Let, $t^{2} = p$

$⇒ 2tdt = dp$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x2}e^{- p}dp$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = 1 - e^{- x^{2}}$

$⇒ 9f \left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9}\right) +$g $\left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9}) ==$9 \left(1 - e^{- \log 9}\right)$

$⇒ 9f \left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9}) +$g \left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9}\right) =9 \left($1 - \dfrac{1}{9}\right)$

$⇒ $9f\left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9}\right) +g\left(\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}9}) =8$

questions.q: Let for some function $\mathrm{y}=f(x), \int_0^x t f(t) d t=x^2 f(x), x\gt0$ and $f(2)=3$. Then $f(6)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int_0^x t f(t) d t=x^2 f(x) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x f(x)=2 x f(x)+x^2 f^{\prime}(x) \\ & \Rightarrow x^2 \cdot f^{\prime}(x)=-x f(x) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}=-\frac{1}{x} \\ & \\ & \quad \int \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x) d x}=-\int \frac{1}{x} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \ln f(x)=-\ln x+C \\ & \\ & \quad f(2)=3 \Rightarrow \ln 3=-\ln 2+C \\ & \quad C=\ln 6 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad f(x)=\frac{6}{x} \Rightarrow f(6)=1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If& $f\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{α}\dfrac{\log_{10}t}{1 + t}dt, \alpha > 0$, then~$f \left(e^{3}\right) + f  \left($e^{- 3}\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

& $f\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{α}\dfrac{\log_{10}t}{1 + t}dt$

So,~$f \left(e^{3}\right) = {∫}_{1}^{e3}\d$dfrac{\ln t}{\ln 10\left(1 + t\right)}dt ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Again~$f\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{α}\dfrac{\ln t}{\left(\ln 10\right)\left(1 + t\right)}dt$

Now let~$t = \dfrac{1}{x}⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{t}⇒ dt = \dfrac{- 1}{x2}dx$

So,~$f \left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{1a}\dfrac{-$lnnx}{ \left(\ln 10\right) \left(1 + $\dfrac{1}{x}\rright)}\left(- \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)$dx$

$⇒ f\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10}{∫}_{1}^{1\alpha}\dfrac{\ln x}{x\left(x + 1\right)}dx$

So,~$f \left($e^{- 3}\right) = $\dfrac{1}{\ln 10}{∫}_{1}^{e3}\dfrac{\ln t}{t \left(t + 1\right)}$dt \ldots \left(2\right)$

Now adding equation~ \left($1\right)$~and~ \left($2\right)$~we get,

f\left($e^{3}\right) + $f\left($e^{- 3}\right)= \left(\dfrac{1}{lnn10}\right){∫}}}_{1}^{c3}\ln t\left(1 + t\right)\left[1 + $\dfrac{1}{t}\right]$dt$

$⇒ f\left(e^{3}\right) + f\left(e^{- 3}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{\ln 10}\right){∫}_{1}^{3}\dfrac{\ln t}{t}dt$

Now let~$\ln t = r⇒ \dfrac{dt}{t} =dr$

So,~$f\left(e^{3}\right) + f\left(e^{- 3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10}{∫}_{0}^{3}rdr$

$⇒ $f \left($e^{3}\right) + $f\left($e^{- 3}\right){= $\left(\dfrac{1}\ln10\right)\left(\dfrac{r2}{2}\right)}_{0}^{3}$

$⇒ f \left($e^{3}\right) + f \left(e^{- 3}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{\log 10}\right)\left(\dfrac{9}{2}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(e^{3}\right) + f\left(e^{- 3}\right) = \dfrac{9}{2\log_{\mathrm{e}}10}$

$

questions.q: $If $f: R \to R$ is a differentiable function and $f  \left(2\right) = 6,$ then $\lim_{x \to 2}{∫}_{6}^{f\left(x\right)}2tdt\left($x - 2\right)$ is:$$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given limit can be written as

$l = \lim_{x \to 2}{∫}_{6}^{f \left(x\right)}2tdt \left($x - 2\right)$

Applying L' Hospital’s rule i.e. if~$l = \lim_{x \to $a}\d$dfrac{g\left(x\right)}{h\left(x\right)}~and~$\lim_{x \to a}$g\left($x\right) \to 0 \text{ and } \lim_{x \to a}$h\left($x\right) \to 0,$~then~$l = \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{g^{'}\left(x\right)}${h^{'}\left($x\right)}$

$l = \lim_{x \to 2}\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}{∫}_{6}^{f\left(x\right)}2tdt}{1}$

Now, applying Newton's Leibnitz rule i.e.~$\dfrac{d}{dx}{∫}}_a^{b}g \left(x\right)dx = g \left(b\right)\cdotb^{'} - $g \left($a\right)$\cdot$a^{'},$~we get

$⇒ l = \lim_{x \to 2} \left($2f \left(x\right) \cdot f^{'}\left(x\right) - 0\right)$

$⇒ l = 2f \left(2\right) ⋅ f^{'} \left($2\right)$

Put the given value, to get

$⇒ l = 2 \times6 \timesf^{'}\left($2\right) = 12f^{'}\left($2\right) .$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_1=\int_{-\frac{1}{2}}^1 2 \mathrm{xf}(2 \mathrm{x}(1-2 \mathrm{x})) \mathrm{dx} \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{dt} \quad \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_1=\frac{1}{2} \int_{-1}^2 \mathrm{tf}(\mathrm{t}(1-\mathrm{t})) \mathrm{dt} \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}_1=\int_{-1}^2(1-\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{f}(1-\mathrm{t})(1-(1-\mathrm{t})) \mathrm{dt} \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}_1=\int_{-1}^2 \mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{t}(1-\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}-\int_{-1}^2 \mathrm{tf}(\mathrm{t}(1-\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}\right. \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}_1=\mathrm{I}_2-2 \mathrm{I}_1 \\ & \Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{I}_1=\mathrm{I}_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{I}_2}{\mathrm{I}_1}=4\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let a differentiable function $f$~satisfy $f \left($x\right) + {∫}_{3}^{x}$\dfrac{f  \left(t\right)}${t}$dt = $\sqrt{x + 1},$x ≥ 3$. Then $12f\left(8\right) is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{3}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{t}dt = \sqrt{x + 1}$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) + $\dfrac{f \left(x\right)}{x} = $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}}$

Put~$y = f\left(x\right)$, then

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}}$

So,~$I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}} = e^{\ln \left|x\right|}$$ = x$

Hence, solution is

$xy = \dfrac{1}{2}∫ \dfrac{x}{x + 1}dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2}∫ $\left(\dfrac{x + 1 - 1}{x + 1})dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2}∫ $\left(\sqrt{x + 1} - \dfrac{1}{x + 1})$dx$

$⇒ xy = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} -2\sqrt{x + 1}\right) +C$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{3} \left($x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \sqrt{x + 1} +$C$

Put~$x = 3$, then~$f\left(3\right) = 2$

So,

$6 = $\dfrac{8}{3} -$2 + C ⇒ C = $\dfrac{16}{3}

Hence,

$xy = $\dfrac{1}{3} \left($x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \sqrt{x + 1} + \dfrac{16}{3}

So, put~$x = 8$, then

$8f\left(8\right) = $\dfrac{27}{3} -$3 + $\dfrac{16}{3}

$⇒ f\left(8\right) = $\dfrac{34}{3 \times 8}

$⇒ 12f\left(8\right) = 17$

$

questions.q: For $x > 0$, if $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{\log_{e}t}{\left(1 + t\right)}dt$, then $f\left(e\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{e}\right)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{\log_{e}t}{\left(1 + t\right)}dt$

$f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = {∫}_{1}^{1 / x}\dfrac{ℓnt}{1 + t}dt$, let $t = \dfrac{1}{y}$

$= {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓn\left(1 / y\right)}{1 + \left(1 / y\right)} . \left(\dfrac{- 1}{y^{2}}\right)dy$

$= + {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓny}{1 + y} . \dfrac{y}{y^{2}}dy$

$= {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓny}{y\left(1 + y\right)}dy$

hence

$f\left(x\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{\left(1 + t\right)ℓnt}{t\left(1 + t\right)}dt = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓnt}{t}dt$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln^{2}\left(x\right)$

so $f\left(e\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{e}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(3\right)$

questions.q: If& $m$ and $n$~respectively are the number of local maximum and local minimum points of the function $f  \left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x2}\dfrac{t^{2} - 5t + 4}{2 + e^{t}}dt$, then the ordered pair \left(m, n\right)$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x2}\dfrac{t^{2} - 5t + 4}{2 + e^{t}}dt$

We know that,

$\dfrac{d}{dx}{∫}_{u \left(x\right)}$^{v\left($x\right)}f\left(v\right)dx = f\left(v \left($x\right)\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}$v \left(u\right) - f \left(u \left($x\right)\right)\d$dfrac{d}{dx}u\left($x\right)$

Using~above formula we get~$f^{'}\left($x\right) = \left(\dfrac{x^{4} - 5x^{2} + 4}{2 + e^{x2}}\right) \cdot$2x$

For critical points~$f^{'}\left($x\right) = 0$

So,~\dfrac{x\left(x^{2} - 1\right)\left(x^{2} - 4\right)}{2 + e^{x2}} =$0$

$⇒ $x\left($x + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)\left($x + 2\right)\left(x - 2\right) = 0$

Now by first derivative test we get,

Here points of maxima are \left\{- 1, 1\right\}$~ &~points of minima are \left\{- 2, 0, 2\right\}$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{x\sin^{8}  x}{\sin^{8}  x + \cos^{8}  x}dx$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $I = {∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{x\sin^{8} x}{\sin^{8} x + \cos^{8} x}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Use the property~${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$~we get,~

$I = {∫}_{0}^{2\ppi}\dfrac{\left($2\pi - x\right)\sin^{8} \left(2\pi - x\right)}{\sin^{8} \left(2\pi - x\right) + \cos^{8} \left(2\pi - x\right)}$dx = {∫}_{0}^{2\ppi}\dfrac{ \left(2\pi - x\right)\sin^{8} x}{\sin^{8} x + \cos^{8} x}$dx . . . \left($ii\right)$

Adding equation~ \left($i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$we get,~

$2I = {∫}_{0}^{2\ppi}\dfrac{2\pi\sin^{8} x}{\sin^{8} x + \cos^{8} x}$dx$

Use the property~${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left($x\right)dx = 2{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left($2a - x\right)dx$~we get,~

$I = 2{∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{\pi\sin^{8} x}${\sin^{8} x + \cos^{8} x}$dx$

Use the property~${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left($x\right)dx = 2{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left($2a - x\right)dx$we get,~

$I = 4{∫}_{0}^{\pi/ 2}$\dfrac{\pi\sin^{8}$ x}{\sin^{8} x + \cos^{8} x}$dx . . . \left(iii\right)$

Use the property~${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$~we get,~

$I = 4{∫}_{0}^{\pi/ $2}\dfrac{\pi\cos^{8}$ x}{\sin^{8} x + \cos^{8} x}dx . . . \left($iv\right)\left($∵ \sin \left(\dfrac{π}{2} -x\right) = \cos x\right)$

Adding the equation~ \left($iii\right) & \left(iv\right)$we get,~

$2I = 4\pi{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}1dx$

$⇒ I = 2\pi{x}_{0}^{\pi / 2} = {π}^{2}$

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\int_0^t t\left(t^2-9 t+20\right) d t, 1 \leq x \leq 5$. If the range of $f$ is $[\alpha, \beta]$, then $4(\alpha+\beta)$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f^{\prime}(x)=x\left(x^2-9 x+20\right), x \in(1,5)=(x-4) x(x-5)$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x) \gt 0 \forall x \in(1,4) \\ & \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x) \lt 0 \forall x \in(4,5) \\ & \Rightarrow f(x) \text { increasing in }(1,4) \\ & \quad f(x) \text { decreasing in }(4,5) \\ & \Rightarrow \text { critical points to check: }\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & x=1,4,5 \\ & f(x)=\int_0^x\left(t^3-9 t^2+20 t\right) d t \\ & =\frac{t^4}{4}-3 t^3+\left.10 t^2\right|_0 ^x=\frac{x^4}{4}-3 x^3+10 x^2 \\ & f(1)=\frac{1}{4}-3+10=\frac{29}{4} \\ & f(4)=4^3-3.4^3+10.4^2=-2.4^3+10.4^2=32 \\ & f(5)=\frac{5^4}{4}-3.5^3+10.25=\frac{5^4}{4}-125=\frac{125}{4}\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \text { Range } \Rightarrow\left[\frac{29}{4}, 32\right] \Rightarrow 4(\alpha+\beta)=128+29 \\ & =157\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{\sin \left(6x\right)}{\sin x}dx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{\sin 6x}{\sin x}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{2\sin 3xcos3x}{\sin x}dx$

$⇒ I = 60{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2\left(3\sin x - 4\sin^{3}x\right)\left(4\cos^{3}x - 3\cos x\right)}{\sin x}dx$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)\left(4\cos^{2}x - 3\right)cosxdx$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)\left(1 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)cosxdx$

Now let $\sin x = t ⇒ cosxdx = dt$ and limit changes to $0\text{to}1$,

So, $I = 120{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(3 - 4t^{2}\right)\left(1 - 4t^{2}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{1}3 - 16t^{2} + 16t^{4}dt$

$⇒ I = 120{\left[3t - \dfrac{16t^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{16t^{5}}{5}\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ I = 120\left[3 - \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{16}{5}\right] = 120 \times \dfrac{45 - 80 + 48}{15} = 8 \times 13 = 104$
questions.question: The value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{\sin \left(6x\right)}{\sin x}dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{\sin 6x}{\sin x}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{2\sin 3xcos3x}{\sin x}dx$

$⇒ I = 60{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2\left(3\sin x - 4\sin^{3}x\right)\left(4\cos^{3}x - 3\cos x\right)}{\sin x}dx$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)\left(4\cos^{2}x - 3\right)cosxdx$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)\left(1 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)cosxdx$

Now let $\sin x = t ⇒ cosxdx = dt$ and limit changes to $0\text{to}1$,

So, $I = 120{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(3 - 4t^{2}\right)\left(1 - 4t^{2}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{1}3 - 16t^{2} + 16t^{4}dt$

$⇒ I = 120{\left[3t - \dfrac{16t^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{16t^{5}}{5}\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ I = 120\left[3 - \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{16}{5}\right] = 120 \times \dfrac{45 - 80 + 48}{15} = 8 \times 13 = 104$

questions.q: The value of& $\dfrac{8}{π}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\left(\cos x\right)2023}{\left(\sin x\right)2023 + \left(\cos x\right)2023}dx$& is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$I = \dfrac{8}{π}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{ \left(\cos x\right)2023}{ \left(\text{ \sin x }\right)2023 + \left(\cos x\right)2023}dx . . . \left($1\right)$

Using~${∫}_{0}^{a}f ( x ) dx = {∫}_{0}^{a}f ( a - x ) dx$

$I = $\dfrac{8}{π}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{ \left(\text{ \sin x }\right)2023}$${ \left(\sin x\right)2023 + \left(\cos x\right)2023}dx . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding~ \left($1\right)$~and~ \left($2\right)$, we get

$2I = \dfrac{8}{π}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}1dx$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{8}{π}{x}_{0}^{\pi2}$

$⇒ I = 2$

questions.q: Let $S = \left(-$1, $\infty\right)$ and f: S \to $\mathbb{R} be defined as $f\left($x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{- 1}^{x}\left($e^{t} - 1\right)11\left($2t - 1\right)5\left($t - 2\right)7\left($t - 3\right)12  \left(2t - 10\right)61dt$. Let $p =$ Sum of square of the values of $x$, where $f\left(x\right)$ attains local maxima on $S$. and $q =$Sum of the values of $x$, where $f  \left(x\right)$ attains local minima on $S$. Then, the value of $p^{2} + 2q$ is ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{- 1}^{x}\left(e^{t} - 1\right)11\left(2t - 1\right)5\left(t - 2\right)7\left(t - 3\right)12\left(2t - 10\right)61dt$

Now, differentiating the above integral using Newton Leibnitz's theorem, we get,

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \left(e^{x} - 1\right)11\left(2x - 1\right)5\left(x - 2\right)7\left(x - 3\right)12\left(2x - 10\right)61$

Now, from the above diagram using first derivative test we get,

Local minima at $x = \dfrac{1}{2}, x = 5$

Local maxima at $x = 0, x = 2$

So, $p = 0 + 4 = 4, q = \dfrac{1}{2} + 5 = \dfrac{11}{2}$

Hence, $p^{2} + 2q = 16 + 11 = 27$

questions.q: For $m, n > 0$, let $\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}t^{m}\left(1 + 3t\right)ndt$. If ,$11\alpha\left(10, 6\right) + 18\alpha\left(11, 5\right) = p\left(14\right)6$, then $p$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}t^{m}\left(1 + 3t\right)ndt$

Now using integration by parts we get,

$⇒ \alpha\left(m, n\right) = {\left(1 + 3t\right)n ⋅ \dfrac{tm + 1}{m + 1}}_{0}^{2} - {∫}_{0}^{2}n\left(1 + 3t\right)n - 1 \times 3 ⋅ \dfrac{tm + 1}{m + 1}dt$

$⇒ \left(m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {\left(1 + 3t\right)n ⋅ \left(t^{m + 1}\right)}_{0}^{2} - 3n\left(m + 1\right){∫}_{0}^{2}\left(1 + 3t\right)n - 1 \times t^{m + 1}dt$

$⇒ \left(m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m, n\right) = \left($1 + 3 $\times$2\right)n ⋅ \left({2}^{m + 1}\right) - 3n \left($m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m + 1, n - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(m + 1\right)\alpha \left(m, n\right) = {7}^{n} \cdot {2}^{m + 1} --3n\alpha\left($m + 1, n - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left($m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m, n\right) + 3n\alpha\left(m + 1, n - 1\right) = {7}^{n} \cdot {2}^{m + 1}$

Now put $m = 10, n = 6$~in above equation we get,

$11\alpha\left(10, 6\right) + 18\alpha\left(11, 5\right) = {7}^{6} \cdot {2}^{11} =32 \times \left(14\right)6$

Hence, on comparing with~$11\alpha\left(10, 6\right) + 18\alpha\left(11, 5\right) = p \times \left(14\right)6$~we get,

$⇒ p = 32$
